newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF says sees reforms stabilising Tokyo stocks.
newsitem.headline: MOF says sees reforms stabilising Tokyo stocks.

text.p: Share prices in Tokyo will stabilise to reflect Japan's economic fundamentals if the market sees Japan's fiscal and economic reforms contributing to stable economic growth, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday.

He said the Japanese government is tackling fiscal and economic structural reforms and deregulation of the financial system in addition to bringing down Japan's high costs in order to achieve stable growth in the medium to longer term.
"If we actively pursue these and manage the economy in such a way we will be able to secure stable and continued growth," he said.
"If our stock market sees these things, the market will stabilise to reflect economic fundamentals," Mitsuzuka said.
Asked about a sharp fall in the New York stock market last week, Mitsuzuka said: "Most see the three percent fall in the New York market as within an adjustment range. I agree with that view."
Japan's economy is continuing its recovery centring on private-sector demand, although the tempo of recovery may be gradual for the time being, he said.

The government's monthly economic report issued earlier this month said domestic demand is becoming firmer and corporate capital spending is on a recovery trend. Mitsuzuka said that according to the report, although the impact of the sales tax rise in April is still lingering, private consumption is on a recovery trend.

Asked about arguments within the government that the Finance Ministry should not handle both fiscal and monetary matters, Mitsuzuka said it was more natural for one administrative body to handle fiscal, monetary and financial system matters, rather than separating them.

Mitsuzuka said his ministry will decide how to deal with debts incurred from the defunct national railways after the Transport Ministry submits budget requests around the end of August for the fiscal year starting next April.
But he added that Japan must tackle fiscal reforms and that just shifting around debts would not lead to a fundamental solution.

Media reports say the Transport Ministry's budget request plans include moving the debts from the national railways, now totalling to around 28 trillion yen, to a special budgetary account and use revenues from government bond issues to cover interest payments. - Tokyo newsroom (813) 3432-8022
